newsitem.title: USA: Senator drops effort to lease US oil shale fields.
newsitem.headline: Senator drops effort to lease US oil shale fields.

text.p: Sen. Ben Nighthorse Campbell dropped a plan to propose opening the U.S. naval oil shale reserves to private oil and gas drilling, a spokeswoman for Campbell said Thursday.

The Colorado Republican had considered introducing an amendment to a defense authorization bill in an attempt to shift control of the naval oil shale reserves in Colorado from the Energy Department to the Interior Department.
Sen. John McCain had been expected to oppose the measure.

Instead of introducing his amendment, Campbell decided to support a similar measure introduced by another Colorado Republican in the House version of the defense bill when the two chambers mesh their provisions.
"We're supporting what (Rep. Joel) Hefley's doing," said Campbell's spokeswoman, Audrey Hudson.
By transferring the property to the Interior Department, the government could lease the mineral rights and split royalties on any production between the federal and state government.
The Energy Department supports the plan, but consumer group Citizen Action has urged lawmakers to oppose it, saying the government should not "give away" the mineral rights.
Citing government studies, Citizen Action said if the government produced and sold natural gas from the reserves itself it could earn more than $83 million for the Treasury.
